title: UNIT 6: ECOLOGY
notes: ✓ Ecology is the study of interactions between organisms and their environment. It explains how living organisms interact with one another and with non-living factors.

title: 6.1.1  Common Ecological Terms
notes:
◆ Ecology → study of organisms and their environment.
◆ Habitat → place where an organism lives.
◆ Population → members of the same species living in an area.
◆ Community → different populations living and interacting in an area.
◆ Ecosystem → community plus its non-living environment.
◆ Biome → large ecological region with characteristic climate, plants and animals.

title: 6.1.2  Biotic and Abiotic Components
notes:
✓ Biotic components are living parts of an ecosystem:
◆ Plants.
◆ Animals.
◆ Microorganisms.

✓ Abiotic components are non-living factors:
◆ Light.
◆ Temperature.
◆ Water.
◆ Air.
◆ Soil.
◆ Minerals.
◆ pH.

Remember: Biotic = living; Abiotic = non-living.

title: 6.1.3  Ecological Levels
notes:
✓ Ecological organization from smaller to larger:

Organism → Population → Community → Ecosystem → Biome → Biosphere.

◆ Organism → one individual.
◆ Population → same species.
◆ Community → different species.
◆ Ecosystem → community + abiotic environment.
◆ Biosphere → all ecosystems on Earth.

title: 6.1.4  Ecosystems
notes:
✓ An ecosystem consists of living organisms and their physical environment interacting as a system.

Main components:
◆ Producers → make food, mainly by photosynthesis.
◆ Consumers → obtain food by eating other organisms.
◆ Decomposers → break down dead organisms and wastes.
◆ Abiotic factors → water, light, temperature, soil and minerals.

→ Energy flows through food chains, while nutrients are recycled.

title: 6.1.5  Biomes
notes:
✓ A biome is a large geographical ecological region characterized mainly by climate and dominant vegetation.

Examples:
◆ Tropical rainforest → hot, wet and highly diverse.
◆ Desert → very dry with sparse vegetation.
◆ Grassland → dominated by grasses.
◆ Savanna → grassland with scattered trees.
◆ Temperate forest → moderate climate with trees.
◆ Tundra → very cold with low-growing vegetation.

title: 6.1.6  Ecological Succession
notes:
✓ Ecological succession is the gradual and predictable change in the species composition and structure of a community over time.

◆ Primary succession → begins on surfaces without soil, such as bare rock.
◆ Secondary succession → occurs where a community was disturbed but soil remains.
◆ Pioneer species → first organisms to colonize an area.
◆ Climax community → relatively stable mature community.

title: 6.2  Ecological Relationships
notes: ✓ Ecological relationships describe interactions between organisms in an ecosystem. They may benefit, harm or have little effect on the organisms involved.

title: 6.2.1  Competition
notes:
✓ Competition occurs when organisms require the same limited resource, such as food, water, space or mates.

Effect → both organisms are negatively affected because they must compete for resources.

Example → plants competing for sunlight and water.

title: 6.2.2  Predation
notes:
✓ Predation is an interaction in which one organism, the predator, captures and eats another organism, the prey.

Effect:
◆ Predator → benefits (+).
◆ Prey → harmed (−).

Example → lion hunting a zebra.

title: 6.2.3  Herbivory
notes:
✓ Herbivory occurs when an animal feeds on plants or plant parts.

Effect:
◆ Herbivore → benefits (+).
◆ Plant → harmed (−).

Example → a cow feeding on grass.

title: 6.2.4  Parasitism
notes:
✓ Parasitism is a relationship in which a parasite lives on or inside a host and obtains nutrients from it.

Effect:
◆ Parasite → benefits (+).
◆ Host → harmed (−).

Example → tapeworm living in the human intestine.

title: 6.2.5  Mutualism
notes:
✓ Mutualism is a relationship in which both organisms benefit.

Effect:
◆ Organism 1 → benefits (+).
◆ Organism 2 → benefits (+).

Example → bees obtain nectar from flowers while helping pollinate them.

title: 6.2.6  Commensalism
notes:
✓ Commensalism is a relationship in which one organism benefits while the other is neither significantly helped nor harmed.

Effect:
◆ Organism 1 → benefits (+).
◆ Organism 2 → unaffected (0).

Example → epiphytic plants growing on trees for support without obtaining nutrients from the tree.

title: UNIT 6 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
Ecology → study of organisms and environment.

Biotic → living factors.
Abiotic → non-living factors.

Organization:
Organism → Population → Community → Ecosystem → Biome → Biosphere.

Interactions:
Competition → − / −
Predation → + / −
Herbivory → + / −
Parasitism → + / −
Mutualism → + / +
Commensalism → + / 0

Succession:
Primary → starts without soil.
Secondary → soil remains after disturbance.

Exam tip: Remember the interaction symbols: + = benefits, − = harmed, 0 = unaffected.
